text.description: From Horseshoe Meadow climb to Mulkey Pass, then follow the crest trail south and leave it for a cross-country climb through foxtail pines and talus to the summit rocks. About 12 miles round trip with roughly 2,900 ft of gain.
Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

Hike in to Long Meadow, leave the trail at an old metal sign and cross the Middle Fork Tule River. Stay just north of the ridge and cut over to the saddle next to point 10,113, then go straight to the summit, avoiding brush.

name: Via Olancha Pass and the PCT

text.description: Climb to Olancha Pass, follow the Pacific Crest Trail north along the west side of the crest, then leave it for the summit. The last stretch is sand, then big granite blocks.

Follow the old road to a wilderness barricade, then a canyon trail to a clearing near 6,100 ft. Take the right fork on a use trail through dark boulders and finish up slabs; about 7 miles round trip with 3,200 ft of gain.
Take the South Fork Big Pine Creek trail to Elinore Lake, climb to the crest at the notch, and follow the ridge to the high pinnacle. A steep class 4 ramp is the key obstacle.

text.description: Hike over Piute Pass, cross Humphreys Basin to the saddle on the east ridge, then scramble boulders to the summit.
A very long trip from Twin Lakes through Kerrick Canyon to Seavey Pass, then up the northeast ridge to a saddle. Drop to a north-side cirque and take a talus chute to the north ridge.

text.description: Reach the cirque of lakes between Black and Red Kaweah from Big Arroyo, then climb the broad west face on loose talus and boulders, keeping well right of Black Kaweah's face. The crest is gained just below the summit; the rock is very unstable. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.
